newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian flag raised over first Belgrade embassy.
newsitem.headline: Croatian flag raised over first Belgrade embassy.

text.p: Croatia formally opened its first-ever embassy in Yugoslavia on Wednesday, improving ties between former enemies that are seen as crucial for keeping an uneasy peace across the Balkans.

Croatia's state news agency HINA said Zvonimir Markovic, Croatian ambassador to Belgrade, handed his credentials to Yugoslav Prime Minister Zoran Lilic and raised the Croatian flag in front of the embassy in the Yugoslav capital's smart Dedinje area.
Croatia fought to secede from Yugoslavia in 1991. The seven-month war, and a subsequent 43-month conflict in Bosnia, left a rump federation comprising Serbia and Montenegro.

Belgrade's relations with its former republic were virtually non-existent until presidents Slobodan Milosevic of Serbia and Franjo Tudjman of Croatia struck a deal on normalisation at a surprise meeting last August.
The Yugoslav ambassador to Croatia has yet to formally present his credentials.
"I am deeply convinced that with this day we are creating a sound basis on which we can build good neighbourly relations," Markovic said.

Serbia and Montenegro have so far refused to divide the assets of former Yugoslavia and they have also sought to block separate deals Croatia and Slovenia negotiatied for their portions of the joint pre-war foreign debt.

Zagreb has long resented the active support the Serbian-dominated Yugoslav Army gave to Croatia's minority Serbs when the latter rebelled against Croatia's independence in 1991 and carved out a self-styled state backed by Belgrade.
